headline: India reopens after Tuesday's Diwali holiday with GIFT Nifty about 1% higher, near 25,300, because Asia and Indian shares in the US rose while India was shut. The rally looks likely to carry on at the open, but rising US interest rates are the cloud over it.

mood.label: Positive
mood.why: Three of the dashboard's four direction checks point up (bias score +30 out of 100); only the put-call ratio check disagrees. Market data is from Monday's close (Tuesday was a holiday); overnight data as of 08:47 IST.

key_points.text: GIFT Nifty (Nifty futures traded overnight in GIFT City) was quoted near **25,309**, about 265 points above Nifty's last close of 25,045, which points to a gap-up open.

While India was closed on Tuesday, Korea's Kospi jumped 4.4% and Japan's Nikkei 2.9%, and Infosys, ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank shares in the US rose 0.7% to 1.6%. Indian stocks have some catching up to do.

US inflation came in hotter than expected on Tuesday. The US 10-year bond rate jumped to about **5.0%** and traders now bet on a Fed rate rise in December, which usually pulls foreign money away from India.
My call: continuation is more likely than a pullback at the open, with medium confidence. It would be proven wrong if Nifty slips back below 25,000 and stays there.
Foreign investors (FIIs) bought **₹7,212 crore** of Indian shares on Monday, about twice their normal daily amount. They have bought about ₹53,000 crore so far in November.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: The night was mostly good for the Indian open and supports the recent rally, but US interest rates moved the wrong way.

points.text: GIFT Nifty near 25,309 suggests Nifty opens about **1% higher**. Analysts quoted by Business Standard expect a gap-up start.
Asia is up again this morning: Taiwan +1.7%, Kospi +1.3%, Nikkei +0.8%. Hong Kong is the exception, down 0.7%.
US stocks fell on Tuesday (S&P 500 −0.4%, Nasdaq −0.7%) after the hot inflation report, but US futures are a little higher this morning (Nasdaq 100 futures **+1.2%** on the day).
The US 10-year bond rate rose 0.12 points to about 5.0%, and the US dollar index rose about 0.5%. Higher US rates and a stronger dollar make India less attractive for foreign money.

Brent crude is about $92, up about **2.7%** since Tuesday evening, but still down about 12% over the past month. Cheaper oil than a month ago is still a big help for India, which imports most of its oil.

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: After a 10% rally in two weeks, I think the rise is more likely to continue at the open than reverse, with medium confidence.

points.text: For continuation: the overnight signals point up, FIIs are still buying hard, and the trend checks are positive. Nifty is above its 20, 50 and 200-day averages.
Option sellers added a lot of new put bets at **25,000** on Monday, which means they expect Nifty to stay above it. The floor moved up from 24,500 to 25,000.
For a pullback: Nifty rose from about 22,700 on 28 Oct to 25,045, a very fast move. Domestic funds (DIIs) sold ₹7,173 crore on Monday, almost exactly what FIIs bought.

FII index-futures long % (the share of their bets that are on a rise) has climbed from 10.6% to **26.8%**. Much of the rushed closing of bets on a fall has already happened, so that fuel is partly used up.
What would prove me wrong: the gap-up fading and Nifty closing below 25,000, or US bond rates rising further.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The dashboard reads the market as moderately bullish, with fear levels higher than usual.

points.text: The data shows Nifty above all three moving averages (20-day 23,374, 50-day 23,283, 200-day 23,988). The swing pattern still reads as a range, because the rally is too new to form fresh swing points.
Futures price and the number of open futures contracts both rose on Monday (open contracts +1.8%), which the dashboard reads as new buying.
The put-call ratio (bets on a fall compared with bets on a rise) fell from 1.40 to **1.23** over five sessions. The dashboard reads that as fewer people protecting against a fall, a mild warning.
India VIX (the market's fear gauge) is 17.4 and rising, higher than 79% of the past year. Fear stays high even as prices rise, so bigger swings are likely both ways.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreign investors have turned into strong buyers, while domestic funds are taking profits.

points.text: FIIs bought for a seventh straight regular session; Monday's ₹7,212 crore came after ₹14,975 crore and ₹13,750 crore last Thursday and Friday.
DIIs (Indian mutual funds and insurers) sold **₹7,173 crore** on Monday and about ₹32,000 crore this month. They are selling into the rally rather than chasing it.
FIIs still hold about 90,700 more bets on a fall than on a rise in index futures, but that gap shrank by 9,700 contracts on Monday.
Reports cite lower crude, cheaper valuations and hopes of a cut in long-term capital gains tax as reasons for the FII buying. I couldn't confirm any official tax decision.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: Cheaper oil than a month ago helps India; a possible US rate rise is the main risk.

points.text: US prices rose faster than expected in October. Traders now see a Fed rate rise in December as very likely; the dashboard flags that 6-month US Treasury bills pay **0.50%** more than the Fed rate.
Brent is down about 12% in a month, which helps India's inflation, its import bill and companies like paints, airlines and oil marketers.
Gold fell about 1.9% on Tuesday as the dollar rose. It matters for jewellers like Titan but has little direct effect on Nifty.
The rupee was about 93.9 per dollar at the last reading (Monday); I couldn't confirm this morning's level.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: Recent Nifty 50 results have been strong, which supports the rally.

points.text: Titan's profit more than doubled (**+114%** vs last year) on 10% higher revenue.
Hindalco profit rose 59% and ONGC 47%; Bharti Airtel profit rose 24% on 17% higher revenue.
Tata Steel profit rose 16% on 12% higher revenue, which the dashboard reads as in line.
No Nifty 50 company is scheduled today. Eicher Motors, Grasim and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles report on Friday, 13 Nov.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: Inflation numbers in India and the US this week matter most.

points.text: India CPI inflation is due on Thursday, 12 Nov at 4 pm. Low inflation would keep hopes of RBI rate cuts alive.
US producer prices on Friday at 7 pm IST: another hot number would push US rates higher and could slow FII buying.
The weekly Nifty expiry is Tuesday, 17 Nov, and the monthly expiry is 23 Nov; markets are shut on 24 Nov.
Any official word on capital gains tax could move the market sharply either way.

levels.note: A close above 25,500 would mean call sellers have given way and the rally has room to run; a close below 25,000 would break the new floor and suggest the rally is tiring.

watch.text: Whether the gap-up holds in the first hour or fades back toward 25,000.
Whether FIIs keep buying in cash and DIIs keep selling; the data comes out in the evening.
US bond rates and US futures during the day; a further jump would weigh on IT and banks.
ECB President Lagarde speaks; mostly a global-mood event.

bottom_line: The dashboard leans bullish (+30), with three of four checks agreeing, and the overnight news points to a higher open as India catches up with Asia's Tuesday rally. Strong FII buying and new put selling at 25,000 support that. The main risks are a very fast 10% rally, heavy selling by domestic funds, and US bond rates near 5% with a Fed rate rise now expected. Confidence is medium: watch whether Nifty holds above 25,000.
